title: Dholavira: a Harappan City
summary: Dholavira is a Harappan city on the arid island of Khadir in Gujarat, occupied between about 3000 and 1500 BCE according to UNESCO. Its fortified city has a heavily fortified castle, a ceremonial ground, streets and houses, a water-management system and a cemetery. The excavator's figures put the walled area at about 771 by 617 m.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO gives occupation between ca. 3000 and 1500 BCE (astronomical -2999 to -1499); the earliest evidence is traced to 3000 BCE in the early Harappan phase.

where.modern_name: Dholavira, Khadir island, Bhachau Taluka, Kachchh, Gujarat, India
where.historical_name: Harappan city on Khadir island, Indus Civilization (ancient name not given in sources)

importance.justification: UNESCO calls it one of the best preserved urban settlements of its period in South Asia.

reviewer_note: No model: the opened pages give the walled area (771.1 x 616.9 m in the arXiv table of the excavator's figures, 771.10 x 616.85 m on Abhijna) but no sourced height, and wall heights in search results came only from slide decks and travel pages. Wall thickness figures (13-18 m) are from a Current Science note and were not used. UNESCO's English text calls the settlement a "city" and says occupation began about 3000 BCE.
